extracted.intended_audience: Investigators preparing an NIH R01 renewal (biomedical researchers in HIV prevention/pharmacology)
extracted.subtask_short: NIH R01 renewal proposal (PrEP hair PK)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparation of an NIH R01 renewal application focused on using pharmacologic measures (hair, plasma, ring residuals) to monitor adherence and pharmacokinetics for PrEP modalities (oral, vaginal ring, long-acting injectables) embedded within large trials. Emphasis on Specific Aims, Research Strategy (Significance, Innovation, Approach), budget justification, human subjects protections, and consortium arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear, hypothesis-driven aims that state primary objectives (e.g., Aim 1: evaluate concentrations of PrEP drugs in hair and plasma as biomarkers and predictors; Aim 2: investigate hair levels as long-term measure of dapivirine exposure and determine threshold associated with low risk; Aim 3: examine utility of hair levels for PK monitoring of long-acting cabotegravir).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims should be concise and directly tied to the overarching goal: develop an integrated package of predictive biologic adherence measures across PrEP delivery methods. Each aim should specify outcomes (e.g., predictors of HIV seroconversion, toxicity), analytic approach (e.g., multivariate models), and relevant subgroups to be examined (e.g., young women, fishermen).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy — Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate the importance of the problem, gaps in current knowledge, and how the proposed work addresses key knowledge gaps (e.g., need for objective pharmacologic adherence metrics during PrEP roll-out and for long-acting modalities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must contextualize within prior trials and public health needs (e.g., lessons from PrEP trials: adherence critical to effectiveness, self-report unreliable, daily dosing challenging). Explain how proposed measures will influence practice paradigms and optimize PrEP delivery in high-incidence settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy — Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly state novel aspects of the proposal (the application lists four innovations: extending hair levels to rings and injectables; incorporating hair measures into a large-scale PrEP study in East Africa; combining short- and long-term adherence measures with triangulation; studying hair as a metric for LA-CAB exposure monitoring).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how the techniques advance the field beyond current practice and address limitations of existing adherence measures (e.g., hair provides long-term integrated exposure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach — Aim-specific experimental design and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide rigorous study design and analysis plans for each aim (e.g., Aim 1 analyze hair and plasma TFV/FTC individually and combined as predictors of seroconversion using multivariate models; Aim 2 compare hair to plasma and residual ring levels and determine an exposure threshold; Aim 3 assess PK variability, segmental hair analysis between injections, and correlations at end of dosing intervals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail sample sources (SEARCH, MTN-025, A5359), statistical methods, subgroup analyses, and plans for triangulation of multiple pharmacologic measures. Include plans for determining thresholds and handling PK tails for injectables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of objective pharmacologic measures and triangulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate objective measures (hair, plasma, residual ring) rather than relying solely on self-report to assess adherence and exposure, and triangulate across measures to characterize patterns (daily, on-demand, drug holidays, white-coat adherence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the rationale and examples (e.g., discordance between plasma and hair may indicate timing of dosing; combined high plasma and hair but low ring suggests recent insertion only). Provide examples of patterns and interpretation to justify planned analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedding measures within ongoing large trials and leveraging collaborations
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage existing trials (SEARCH, MTN-025/HOPE, ACTG A5359) and include trial leadership as collaborators to ensure integration and access to specimens and outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how collaborating with trial chairs/co-investigators improves feasibility, sample size, and generalizability. Budget and document roles/effort (e.g., co-investigators commit calendar months/effort).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator qualifications and role/effort allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Document that key personnel have relevant expertise, track record, and committed effort (e.g., biosketch-like narrative for Drs. Baeten, Castillo-Mancilla with specified calendar months and responsibilities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe mentoring plans for early career investigators, detail specific responsibilities (e.g., oversee hair collection, data analysis, manuscript preparation), and quantify effort (% or calendar months) for personnel and trainees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary data and feasibility (prior productivity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide prior work demonstrating feasibility and productivity (e.g., 20 papers from the first grant demonstrating hair measures utility; prior analyses showing detectable levels in hair/plasma).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prior results to justify study rationale and feasibility (e.g., hair levels predict outcomes, prior assays and methods established).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimen collection, QA oversight, and shipping
rubrics_metrics.description: Define standard procedures and quality assurance for specimen collection (hair, plasma, used rings), including oversight visits to field sites and specifying shipping arrangements back to central lab (e.g., travel by PI/QA coordinator to supervise collection; estimated shipping costs per year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget personnel travel for on-site oversight, describe collection training, specify shipment frequency/costs, and explain how specimen integrity will be maintained and monitored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample analysis infrastructure: equipment lease and service agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify equipment needs and costs for assay validation and sample analysis (e.g., LC-MS/MS lease and annual service agreements apportioned by year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide cost breakdowns per year, proportion costs according to project aims/time of use, and include service contracts for maintenance. Explain why leasing (vs purchase) is chosen and how costs are allocated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget justification — travel (international and domestic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear justification for travel costs: purpose (oversight, conferences), destinations, duration (e.g., 10-day site visits), personnel traveling, and per-trip cost estimates for airfare, lodging, meals, local transport.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish international site visits (oversight of specimen collection; attendance at SEARCH retreat) from domestic conference travel (CROI, MTN meetings, ACTG meeting), specify years covered and total per-year travel budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget justification — publication, consultant, and other direct costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Include planned publication costs by year, consultant costs, and other direct costs (e.g., specimen shipping, tuition for graduate student), with totals over project period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List annual amounts and explain necessity (e.g., publication fees in years 2–5), include consultant scope and justification, and document trainee tuition/fringe calculations where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget justification — institutional recharges and allowable direct costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Document institutional recharges (UCSF Data & Network recharge, CCDSS) and justify them as allowable direct expenses per cognizant federal agency guidance (cite DHHS Division of Cost Allocation and applicable OMB requirements like 2 CFR Part 220).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide per capita recharge rates, effective dates, and note that rates will be reviewed annually. Direct reviewers to agency contact for questions and include how charges are apportioned by effort/FTE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe benefits, tuition, and F&A rate documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply and document institutional fringe benefit rates, tuition estimates for trainees, and negotiated F&A (indirect cost) rates with citation to the DHHS negotiated rate agreement and how MTDC is defined and applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify which costs are excluded from MTDC (e.g., tuition), state effective dates and projected increases in F&A if applicable, and show calculations per year for transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects protections and related documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Protection of Human Subjects section, indicate whether the project is a clinical trial, include a Data Safety Monitoring Plan, and address inclusion of women/minorities and children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State if the project involves a clinical trial, attach a DSM plan, explain protections and plans to include diverse populations, and include required forms and PDFs (ProtectionOfHumanSubjects, DataSafetyMonitoringPlan, InclusionWomenMinorities, InclusionOfChildren).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Income disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether program income is anticipated and, if so, provide anticipated amounts, budget periods, and sources in the specified format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 'Yes', complete the table with budget period, anticipated amount ($), and source(s); otherwise leave blank. Follow PHS 398 instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate animals and AVMA euthanasia compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose whether vertebrate animals are used/euthanized and if so, confirm methods are consistent with AVMA guidelines or provide justification for deviations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the Vertebrate Animals section and, if euthanasia is used, indicate AVMA compliance or give scientific justification for alternative methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human embryonic stem cell disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the project involves human embryonic stem cells; if yes, list registration numbers or indicate a registered line will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow PHS 398 Cover Page Supplement instructions and reference the NIH stem cell registry when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions and patents reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose whether inventions or patents exist related to the project and whether they were previously reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer the Inventions and Patents section (Yes/No) and provide details per renewal instructions when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium/Contractual arrangements and letters of support
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed consortium agreements/contractual arrangements and letters of support documenting roles, responsibilities, and subaward budgets (ConsortiumArrangements, LettersOfSupport).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include subaward direct costs and F&A in summaries, show how partner institutions contribute, and include signed letters that confirm commitment and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource sharing and authentication of key biological/chemical resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide Resource Sharing Plan(s) and Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources documentation to ensure reproducibility and accessibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach plans for data/sample sharing, repositories, and procedures to authenticate reagents, cell lines, and assays to be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix content and allowable materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Include appropriate Appendix materials as permitted by NIH policy (e.g., appendices_Gandhi_R01rnwl.pdf), following page limits and allowed content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure appendices do not contain disallowed introductory or preliminary data beyond NIH rules; include only permitted documents (e.g., blank consent forms, protocol documents) and reference them in the Research Plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis plans and subgroup analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Present detailed statistical analysis plans, including multivariate modeling, predictors selection, and prespecified subgroup analyses (e.g., young women, mobile populations, clinic vs home delivery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify outcome definitions (e.g., HIV seroconversion), power/ sample size considerations or justification via embedding in large trials, and methods for handling missing data and discordant biomarkers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defining and validating biomarker thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Define plans to determine exposure thresholds in biomatrices (e.g., a hair dapivirine threshold associated with low HIV risk) and validate these thresholds using trial outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe analytic approaches and criteria for threshold selection, cross-validation across matrices (hair/plasma/ring residual), and how thresholds will inform monitoring in roll-out settings.
